dossier.public_summary: A 0.5-day dip recurs on this M-dwarf but the measured depth changes by more than a factor of two between sectors taken with the same pipeline and the star shows a strong 3-day brightness swing of amplitude larger than the dip itself. The dip is centred on the target, so the signal is the star’s own spotted variability / pulsation rather than a background binary or a planet. The duration and large out-of-transit swing are inconsistent with a 1.9 Earth-size planet.

reasons.why: depth changes by >100% between two SPOC sectors (same source). Phase-curve amplitude 1346 ppm (ratio_to_depth 0.6128, chi2 63.14 dof 7) is larger than the 2196 ppm dip, consistent with stellar variability not a planet.
reasons.value: 3.638e-11 depth_change_pct 104.7 per sector 908 ppm vs 2903 ppm

reasons.why: tool shows depth change is real within one light-curve product, ruling out calibration as explanation.

dip period is ~1/6 of the strong 3.05 d spot period with huge variability; favours spots/background binary over planet. Duration ratio 1.635 and star_density_penalty 69.01 are inconsistent with a central planet.
